title: The derived Poincaré pairing is the duality isomorphism
statement:
Let $X$ satisfy the hypotheses of [sk-thm-sf-global-duality],
with the orientation of [sk-def-sf-orientation] fixed, and let
$K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ be perfect over $\Lambda_X$ [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Then the tensor–internal-Hom
adjoint of the derived pairing [def-sf-pairing]

$$
\beta_K:\RG_c(X,K)\otimes^L_\Lambda\RG\bigl(X,K^\vee(d)\bigr)[2d]\to\Lambda
$$

is the canonical isomorphism
$\RG(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim} R\mathrm{Hom}_\Lambda(\RG_c(X,K),\Lambda)$ *in the point category*
$\Dbc(s,\Lambda)$, and its inverse is the global
duality isomorphism of [sk-thm-sf-global-duality] followed by
$\mathbb D_XK\cong K^\vee(d)[2d]$. In particular $\beta_K$ is perfect.
If $X$ is proper and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},E,\Qlb\}$, its degreewise form
gives perfect pairings
$\langle-,-\rangle_i:H^i_c(X,K)\times H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))\to\Lambda$
(over $A_{E,n}$ because this ring is self-injective, so
$\operatorname{Hom}(-,\Lambda)$ is exact). At the integral stage
$\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ the degreewise form fails in general: a torsion
class in $H^i_c$ pairs to zero with everything, and
$H^{-i}(\RG_c^\vee)$ picks up an $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ term from the
torsion of $H^{i+1}_c$; only the derived statement holds there.

proof.text: Write $a=a_X$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $C=R\Gamma_c(X,K)$, $T=\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ and $L=K^\vee(d)[2d]=K^\vee\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}T$ (derived shift identifications). The coefficient dual of a site-perfect $K$ is site-perfect by [prop-sf-dualizable], so the pairing [def-sf-pairing] is defined with its required hypothesis on $K^\vee$. Let $\gamma:T\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra^!\Lambda_s$ be the fixed orientation [sk-def-sf-orientation], read through $La^*\Lambda_s\cong\Lambda_X$. By [prop-sf-dualizable-hom] at $M=T$, the evaluation comparison $\tau':L=K^\vee\otimes^LT\to R\mathcal Hom_X(K,T)$, the tensor–internal-Hom transpose of $\operatorname{ev}_K(d)[2d]:K\otimes^LL\to T$, is an isomorphism; its inverse is the twist identification $R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X(d)[2d])\cong K^\vee(d)[2d]$ of [sk-lem-sf-twist-interchange] ($m=d$, $n=2d$). Put $j=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\gamma)\circ\tau':L\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb D_XK=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,Ra^!\Lambda_s)$ and $\theta=j^{-1}$; this is the identification $\mathbb D_XK\cong K^\vee(d)[2d]$ of the statement. By naturality of the transpose in the target, $j$ is the transpose of $e=\gamma\circ\operatorname{ev}_K(d)[2d]:K\otimes^LL\to Ra^!\Lambda_s$, i.e. $\operatorname{ev}_{\mathbb D_XK}\circ(1_K\otimes j)=e$. The global-duality isomorphism of [sk-thm-sf-global-duality] is $G:C^\vee\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X,\mathbb D_XK)$; its construction is recalled and compared in Step 6. Thus $B=R\Gamma(\theta)\circ G:C^\vee\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X,L)=R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]$ is the specified inverse candidate.

Expand the tensor-Hom exchange of [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom] at $f=a$, $M=K$, $N=\Lambda_s$, using the adjunctions and projection formula (A1), (A3) of [def-sf-datum]. For an arbitrary test object $V$ in the constructible finite-Tor point category, a map $v:V\to Ra_*L$ has pullback transpose $\widetilde v=\varepsilon^*_{L}\circ La^*v:La^*V\to L$. Under the chain
$$\operatorname{Hom}_s(V,Ra_*L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(La^*V,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(K\otimes^L La^*V,Ra^!\Lambda_s)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(Ra_!(K\otimes^L La^*V),\Lambda_s)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(Ra_!K\otimes^L V,\Lambda_s),$$
$v$ is sent to the explicit map
$$\varepsilon^!_{\Lambda_s}\circ Ra_!\bigl(e\circ(1_K\otimes\widetilde v)\bigr)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{a,K,V}.$$
Here the middle internal-Hom identification is $j$, the third bijection is the exceptional adjunction, and the last map precomposes with the projection isomorphism. These are precisely the unit/counit formulas for adjunction: no assertion about mates of composition is needed. All objects tested are in the finite-Tor domain of (A1), (A3); no ambient right adjoint on all pro-etale complexes is invoked.

source.place: proof, second sentence: expand the tensor-Hom chain at M=K, N=Lambda, f=a_X

proof.text:
By the definition [def-sf-cup], cup product is the projection transformation followed by $Ra_!(1_K\otimes\varepsilon^*_{L})$. By [def-sf-pairing], the remaining maps are the twisted evaluation and $\varepsilon^!_{\Lambda_s}\circ Ra_!(\gamma)$. Naturality of the projection transformation in its second variable gives
$$\beta_K\circ(1_{Ra_!K}\otimes v)=\varepsilon^!_{\Lambda_s}\circ Ra_!\bigl(e\circ(1_K\otimes(\varepsilon^*_{L}\circ La^*v))\bigr)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{a,K,V}.$$
The right side is the image of $v$ under the explicit tensor–Hom exchange chain of [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom] at $f=a$, $M=K$, $N=\Lambda_s$. Taking $V=Ra_*L$ and $v=1$ shows that the point curry of the pairing is
$$\Phi=b_1\circ Ra_*j,$$
where $b_1$ is the exchange map at $\Lambda_s$.

source.place: proof, Step 3: evaluate the adjunction chain and identify the point curry

proof.text:
At the finite coefficient stage $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, apply [lem-sf-identification-coefficient-transport] with $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_s,a}$ the finite compact-support composition comparison, which that statement normalizes to the identity under $R\mathrm{id}_{s!}\cong\mathrm{id}$. Thus $
u:\omega_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_s$ is an isomorphism, $c=Ra^!(
u)$, and $\varepsilon^!_{\Lambda_s}\circ Ra_!(c)=
u\circ\varepsilon^!_{\omega_s}$.

source.place: proof, Step 3: the point counit normalization and the conjugate composition mate

proof.text:
At each of the integral, rational and common-stage coefficient domains, [lem-sf-identification-coefficient-transport] states that the specified completed or scalar-transferred comparison $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_s,a}:R\mathrm{id}_{s!}Ra_!	o Ra_!$ of [fix-lem-exchanges](2),(4) is the identity under $R\mathrm{id}_{s!}\cong\mathrm{id}$. Its conclusion gives the counit isomorphism $
u:\omega_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_s$, the mate $c=Ra^!(
u)$ and the equation $\varepsilon^!_{\Lambda_s}\circ Ra_!(c)=
u\circ\varepsilon^!_{\omega_s}$ in the actual category at that stage. These are precisely the normalization identities needed below; the node asserts them for the specified completed comparison, rather than deducing an integral equation from equality of its finite reductions.

source.place: proof, second sentence: identity-point composition normalization; fix-lem-exchanges (2),(4) at (id_s,a)

proof.text:
Apply the naturality comparison of [lem-sf-identification-exchange-comparison], with its all-stage point-counit normalization supplied by [lem-sf-identification-coefficient-transport], to the two tensor–Hom exchanges. It gives
$$b_1\circ Ra_*R\mathcal Hom_X(K,c)=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\nu)\circ b_{\omega},$$
so the Verdier exchange used in [sk-thm-sf-global-duality] is $\eta_K=b_1^{-1}\circ R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\nu)$. The same node gives
$$\alpha_C=\alpha_C^1\circ\operatorname{Fib}_sR\mathcal Hom_s(C,\nu),\qquad G=\operatorname{Fib}_s(b_1^{-1})\circ(\alpha_C^1)^{-1}.$$
Thus the construction of global duality agrees with the exchange at $\Lambda_s$, after the normalized point comparison.

source.place: proof, Step 3: naturality of tensor–Hom in N and comparison with global duality

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sf-identification-fibre-adjunction] to the point pairing of Step 3, with $P=Ra_!K$, $Q=Ra_*L$ and its curry $\Phi$; its $\alpha_P^1$ is the comparison denoted $\alpha_C^1$ here. The coherent tensor and unit comparisons read that point pairing in the coefficient category. For the actual coefficient pairing of [def-sf-pairing], its adjoint is
$$\beta_K^\sharp=\alpha_C^1\circ\operatorname{Fib}_s(\Phi).$$
Combining this with $\Phi=b_1\circ Ra_*j$ from Step 3 and with the formula for $G$ above yields
$$\beta_K^\sharp=G^{-1}\circ R\Gamma(j)=B^{-1},$$
where $B=R\Gamma(\theta)\circ G$ is the inverse candidate of Step 1. Since $G$ and $R\Gamma(\theta)$ are isomorphisms, the adjoint is an isomorphism and the pairing is perfect.

source.place: proof, Step 3: passage from the point curry to the coefficient pairing and conclusion

proof.text:
Assume $X$ proper and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. The point equivalence [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence] reads $C$ as a bounded complex with finite cohomology over $\Lambda$ (a common finite-stage complex at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$). By clause 1 of [lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius], $\Lambda$ is injective over itself and ordinary $D=\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(-,\Lambda)$ is exact, with finite-module biduality. The complex $\Lambda[0]$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], so the definition [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] computes $C^\vee$ by $D(P)^j=\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(P^{-j},\Lambda)$ for a complex representative $P$ of $C$, with differential $d^j(f)=(-1)^{j+1}f d_P^{-j-1}$. Exactness and [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology], applied to the opposite module category and with degrees reversed, give the canonical evaluation-induced isomorphism
$$H^{-i}(C^\vee)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(H^i(C),\Lambda).$$
This works for the finite quotient ring as well as for the two fields; it does not assume that the individual cohomology modules are projective. At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ the computation is made at a common finite field stage and interpreted in the finite-stage category of the point equivalence.

source.place: proof, last sentence: exact coefficient duality and cohomology of the dual

proof.text:
Apply $H^{-i}$ to $\beta_K^\sharp$ from Step 7 and then to the canonical identification of Step 8. The shift convention gives $H^{-i}(R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d])=H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))$, hence
$$H^{2d-i}(X,K^\vee(d))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(H_c^i(X,K),\Lambda).$$
The arrow evaluates a class against a class of $H_c^i$, because both its factors are induced by the evaluation used in $\beta_K$. Thus it is the adjoint of the stated degreewise pairing. The other adjoint is also an isomorphism: dualize this arrow and compose with the finite-module evaluation isomorphism of [lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius]. This proves perfectness, including when one or both groups vanish and when the finite-coefficient groups are not free.

source.place: proof, last sentence: apply H^{-i} and the shift convention

proof.text: For the integral warning put $R=\mathcal O_E$ and $\pi=\varpi_E$. It is a DVR by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. The point equivalence [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence] makes $C$ a bounded finite-cohomology $R$-complex, and clause 2 of [lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius] makes it perfect. Choose a bounded finite-projective representative $P$ using [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Its terms are finite free: a finite generating list gives a surjection $R^r\to P^i$, which splits by the lifting definition [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]; apply [lem-sc-dvr-saturation-line-smith-normal-form] to its image in $R^r$. The same Smith theorem makes $Z^i=\ker(d_P^i)$ and $B^i=\operatorname{im}(d_P^{i-1})$, submodules of $P^i$, finite free. By [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective], $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_R(P,-)$ takes acyclic complexes to acyclic complexes. For a K-injective resolution $R[0]\to I$, its cone is acyclic, and the cone of $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,R[0])\to\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,I)$ is $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,\operatorname{Cone}(R[0]\to I))$ with the usual cone signs. It is acyclic. Thus [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] computes $C^\vee$ by the ordinary dual complex $D(P)$ also in this integral case; this is the explicit projective-source argument of Stacks Tag 0A66, not an assumption that $R$ is self-injective.

source.place: Tag 0A66, lemma-RHom-out-of-projective; Tag 07VI, lemma-dual-perfect-complex; integral warning of the item statement

proof.text:
A degree $-i$ dual cocycle is a functional $P^i\to R$ vanishing on $B^i$. Restriction to $Z^i$ defines $H^{-i}(D(P))\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(H^i(P),R)$; dual boundaries restrict to zero. It is onto because $P^i/Z^i=B^{i+1}$ is free, so $Z^i\subset P^i$ splits by [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Its kernel is
$$\operatorname{Hom}_R(B^{i+1},R)\big/\operatorname{im}\bigl(\operatorname{Hom}_R(P^{i+1},R)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(B^{i+1},R)\bigr).$$
Since $Z^{i+1}\subset P^{i+1}$ also splits, the image in this quotient equals the image of $\operatorname{Hom}_R(Z^{i+1},R)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ext-long-exact-first-variable] to $0\to B^{i+1}\to Z^{i+1}\to H^{i+1}(P)\to0$; [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ext-criterion] gives $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(Z^{i+1},R)=0$. The quotient is therefore $\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(H^{i+1}(P),R)$, proving
$$0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(H_c^{i+1}(X,K),R)\to H^{-i}(C^\vee)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(H_c^i(X,K),R)\to0.$$
The Smith diagonal form of $B^{i+1}\subset Z^{i+1}$ [lem-sc-dvr-saturation-line-smith-normal-form] identifies this Ext cokernel with the sum of $R/(a_j)$ for its nonzero diagonal scalars $a_j$; its free summands contribute zero. Thus this term comes precisely from torsion in $H_c^{i+1}$, as claimed.

source.place: Tags 0A66 and 07VI, dual complex calculation; explicit cycles/boundaries calculation for the integral warning

proof.text: Every $R$-bilinear pairing into the domain $R$ kills torsion: if $0\ne a\in R$ annihilates $x$, then $a\beta(x,y)=\beta(ax,y)=0$, hence $\beta(x,y)=0$. Failure actually occurs under the theorem's hypotheses. Take $X=s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $d=0$, and $K=(R/\pi R)_s$ in degree zero. It is perfect, represented by $[R_s\xrightarrow{\pi}R_s]$ in degrees $-1,0$; $X$ is smooth, proper and geometrically connected. Here $H_c^0(X,K)=R/\pi R\ne0$, while the dual of that two-term complex has cohomology zero in degree $0$ and $R/\pi R$ in degree $1$. Thus the degree-zero pairing has a nonzero first factor and zero second factor, and is not perfect. Equivalently the Ext term of Step 11 is nonzero for $i=-1$, whereas ordinary duality annihilates $H_c^0$. The nonzero quotient and cancellation by $\pi$ use the DVR statement [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. The derived isomorphism of Steps 1–7 remains valid, so the integral warning concerns precisely the degreewise conclusion and does not alter the derived result.
